newsitem.title: USA: 3M says wins Memphis breast implant case.
newsitem.headline: 3M says wins Memphis breast implant case.

text.p: Minnesota Mining and Manufacturing Co said on Friday that a Memphis, Tennessee jury ruled in its favor in a breast implant case.

The jury decided after six hours of deliberation that Minnesota Mining should not be held liable for allegations by the plaintiff, Sandra Tyson, that her breast implants caused her to have health problems, Minnesota Mining said.
This is the second time in the past year that a jury has found in favor of the company, Minnesota Mining said, adding that in a third case, the jury was deadlocked.

"We are extremely pleased by the verdict," said Dr Carol Ley, associate medical director for the company. "It means that science is having its day in court, with a legal decision supporting what the medical community has determined. The well-controlled scientific studies on breast implants, which number at least 16, have found no association between silicone gel breast implants and disease.
"We sympathize with anyone who is ill," Ley said in a news release. "But this suit and others like it are not based on scientific evidence."
Shares of Minnesota Mining rose 3/8 to 72-1/2.
